executive_summary: The 'Check for Filesystem Drift' CI job's own drift-detection step carried both an exit-zero fallback and continue-on-error:true, so the job could never actually fail on real drift -- only earlier checkout/setup/install/compile steps could fail it. A real recent red run was a CDN connection reset during an unrelated puppeteer postinstall, not drift, teaching readers that a red run of this check means noise rather than drift. Fixed by removing both suppressions so the underlying tools/gates/drift-check.ts script's real exit code now propagates as the job's own status, verified currently a no-op (zero real violations across all three severity:'critical' patterns) so this promotion cannot newly block any merge.

functional_requirements.title: Promote the drift-detection step's real exit code to the job's own status
functional_requirements.description: .github/workflows/leo-drift-check.yml's 'Run drift detection' step wrapped `node dist/tools/gates/drift-check.js` in `|| { echo ...; exit 0; }` and also carried `continue-on-error: true` -- two independent suppressions stacked on the same step. Remove both so a real drift-check.js exit(1) genuinely fails the job.
acceptance_criteria: The 'Run drift detection' step no longer contains an `|| { ... exit 0; }` fallback.
The step no longer has `continue-on-error: true`.
The step's `run:` is the bare `node dist/tools/gates/drift-check.js` invocation.

functional_requirements.title: Verify the promotion is currently a no-op before shipping (never guess)
functional_requirements.description: drift-check.ts has three severity:'critical' checks that can trigger exit(1): prd_files, handoff_files, and boundary_violations (a regex-based cross-repo import scan). Each must be independently verified as currently zero-violation on this repo before promoting, since a mistaken promotion would newly break CI for everyone.
acceptance_criteria: git ls-files shows zero tracked matches for prd_files' patterns (prds/**/*.md, prds/**/*.txt).

handoff_files' raw glob (docs/**/handoff-*.md, handoffs/**/*.md) is checked directly, and any real matches are cross-checked against drift-check.ts's own ALLOWLIST_PATTERNS ('docs/**/*.md' etc.) to confirm none actually violate -- not merely assumed absent.

boundary_violations' two import-direction regex scans (LEO files importing /venture|/portfolio|/src, and App files importing /leo|/validation|scripts/leo) are replayed directly (grep or equivalent) and confirmed zero matches.

functional_requirements.title: Confirm the promotion cannot newly block any PR merge
functional_requirements.description: Before shipping, confirm 'Check for Filesystem Drift' is not itself a required branch-protection status check, so promoting its own status to be honest carries no risk of newly blocking a merge that previously succeeded.
acceptance_criteria: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks` is queried directly and its `contexts` array does not include 'Check for Filesystem Drift'.

functional_requirements.title: Regression-proof the fix with a source-pinned, mutation-verified test
functional_requirements.description: Add a test that reads the workflow YAML source directly and asserts the drift-detection step no longer contains the fallback/continue-on-error pattern, so a future edit cannot silently reintroduce it.
acceptance_criteria: A new test file asserts the step's text does not match `|| {`, `exit 0`, or `continue-on-error: true` within the drift-detection step specifically.
Mutation-verified: reverting the fix (stash/checkout the old text) makes the new test fail; restoring the fix makes it pass again.

technical_requirements.description: No schema changes. This is a CI workflow YAML edit plus one new unit test file; no production application code touched.

Scoped strictly to the drift-check job's one step. The sibling boundary-check job carries an identical exit-zero + continue-on-error pattern and is deliberately left untouched -- a separate concern not named by this fix.

The workflow's own inline comment documenting the promotion's rationale must itself be evidence-accurate -- an independent VALIDATION sub-agent review found and required correction of two factual errors in the first draft (a false 'zero tracked matches' claim for handoff_files, and an incomplete severity-pattern list omitting boundary_violations).

test_scenarios.scenario: The drift-detection step's source text is inspected directly
test_scenarios.expected: No exit-zero fallback, no continue-on-error:true, and the run command is the bare drift-check.js invocation.

test_scenarios.scenario: The fix is reverted (mutation test) and the new regression test is re-run
test_scenarios.expected: The test fails, proving it genuinely discriminates the fixed state from the original broken state.

test_scenarios.scenario: Branch protection required_status_checks is queried for the live repo
test_scenarios.expected: 'Check for Filesystem Drift' does not appear in the required contexts list, confirming this promotion cannot newly block any PR.

risks.risk: A future PR could introduce a real prd_files/handoff_files/boundary_violations match, and the newly-honest job status would (correctly) turn red for the first time in a long while, surprising a reader unfamiliar with this change.
risks.mitigation: That is the intended, correct behavior this fix restores -- a red 'Check for Filesystem Drift' finally means drift again. Documented in the workflow's own inline comment and this PRD for future readers.

risks.risk: handoff_files' critical pattern is unreachable by construction today (every real match also matches the broad docs/**/*.md allowlist), so this promotion provides zero real protection for that specific pattern.
risks.mitigation: Out of scope for this fix -- flagged as a completion-flag finding for future follow-up, not silently left undocumented.

consumers: Any GitHub Actions run of leo-drift-check.yml's drift-check job, on push to main/develop or on a pull_request touching tools/gates/**, scripts/**, lib/**, .eslintrc*, package.json, or the workflow file itself
runtime_config: No new env vars or config flags
observability_rollout: No feature flag needed -- ships in one deploy; the job's own status becomes honest immediately post-merge, currently green given zero real violations
